text:
Sophie Li: seeing a sudden p99 regression for model-inference in eastus-2 around 09:12-09:28 UTC. latency graphs + error rate spike. looks correlated with host egress drops on a subset of GPU nodes. :eyes:
Alex Chen: can you paste `tc qdisc show` from one affected host?
Sophie Li: pasted below from host gpu-e-12 (shortened):
```
$ sudo tc qdisc show dev eth2
qdisc fq_codel 0: limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 3000 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms
qdisc ingress ffff: parent ffff:fff1 ----------------
```
Sophie Li: noticed quantum is 3000 which is higher than our default, also saw lots of redispatch/drop stats when I ran `tc -s qdisc`
Alex Chen: weird, we don't set quantum anywhere in our baseline. did a config run from the qos role happen? @config-bot any recent runs?
config-bot: chef-client run completed on gpu-e-12 at 2026-03-12T09:09:58Z. Applied recipes: `host-qos::enable-fq_codel`, `net-tuning::egress-throttle`.
Jamal Patel: that chef recipe was supposed to set quantum=1514 (link MTU). If quantum changed to 3000 that could increase burst size and interact badly with NIC GRO/TSO leading to reordering + drops.
Kevin O'Neill: if packets get coalesced by TSO/GRO then fq_codel might see large packets and start redispatching, which could spike p99 for websocket / gRPC streams.
Maria Gómez: quick mitigation: can we revert the recipe or push a fix to set quantum back to 1514?
Alex Chen: I'm SSHing to the node now to toggle off fq_codel and re-run tests.
Alex Chen: ran `sudo tc qdisc replace dev eth2 root fq_codel quantum 1514` -> re-ran synthetic load against local inference instance: p99 dropped from 340ms -> 95ms.
Sophie Li: confirmed on the incident graph: model-p99 in that AZ trended back down ~2 minutes after change. :thumbsup:
Jamal Patel: we should also check for interactions with NIC offloads. please run `ethtool -k eth2` on a couple of hosts.
Sophie Li: `ethtool -k eth2` shows tso on, gso on, gro on.
Kevin O'Neill: short term: keep quantum=1514 and add note to disable QoS recipe until we audit. Long term: adjust recipe to set quantum based on actual MTU and include a preflight check for offload settings.
Maria Gómez: filing a little follow-up ticket: "host-qos: ensure quantum aligned to MTU and avoid large quantum with TSO/GRO". tagging infra oncall.
config-bot: rolling back host-qos recipe in fleet-eastus2 at 2026-03-12T09:20:12Z (initiative rollback).
monitoring-bot: alert cleared: inference-p99-eastus2 (was firing for 16m) at 2026-03-12T09:24:33Z.
Sophie Li: couple of takeaways: 1) don't hardcode quantum > MTU, 2) instrument `tc -s qdisc` to ship per-host qdisc stats into our metrics exporter, 3) add a preflight check in chef to assert NIC offload compatibility.
Alex Chen: adding a short playbook to run during on-call: `tc qdisc show`, `tc -s qdisc`, `ethtool -k`, `sudo tc replace ...` + graph link.
Jamal Patel: also flagging this as a small runbook change for Private deployments — some customers have different MTUs, we should be cautious.
Maria Gómez: noted. I'll own a short postmortem doc with timeline and the PR to fix the recipe.
Sophie Li: thanks folks — closing the thread once the PR lands. :white_check_mark:
